A1.justification: Both PDFs describe DRE-BO-SSL. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v3 reports original optimization experiments on synthetic functions, Tabular Benchmarks, NATS-Bench, and multi-digit MNIST, plus sensitivity studies in the appendices.

after.justification: v4 retains these original experiments and appendix analyses and additionally reports results for the protein-structure Tabular Benchmark.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same label propagation/spreading, entropy-based kernel-parameter fitting, unlabeled-point sampling, pool handling, and acquisition maximization with random tie handling. Expanded equation displays do not change the procedure.

E1.justification: Section 5.2 and Figure 5 add reported evaluation on protein structure. v3 names and plots only naval propulsion, Parkinsons, and slice localization, despite referring to four Tabular datasets. All other datasets and task scenarios are retained.

E2.justification: Both versions compare against GP-EI/UCB and BORE/LFBO using random forests, gradient boosting, XGBoost, and MLPs. The new Protein panel uses this same comparator set, and the Appendix A comparisons are retained.

E3.justification: The retained experiments preserve their metrics, search spaces, pool sizes, and optimization and training settings. Protein extends the existing Tabular protocol. The explicit five-point initialization in v4 is newly disclosed information, without evidence that an existing protocol changed.

E4.justification: The classifier illustrations and analyses of kernel parameter beta, unlabeled-point counts and sampling distributions, pool subset sizes, and threshold ratio remain unchanged. The runtime analysis moves from v3 Figure 8 to v4 Figure 14 in Appendix G.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments use 20 repetitions with 20 fixed random seeds and report sample means and standard errors. The added Protein results follow the existing reporting practice.

E6.justification: v4 Figure 5(b) adds mean-squared-error trajectories for Protein for DRE-BO-SSL and the existing baselines. Previously reported figure panels retain their results, and the MNIST classifier accuracies remain 99.6%, 97.0%, and 96.9% for training, validation, and test data.

T1.justification: Assumption 4.1, Definition C.1, and the mathematical reasoning remain unchanged. v4 converts existing inline expressions into numbered equations and separates the two updates in v3 Equation 7 into Equations 11–12; it adds no new mathematical result or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims: identify over-exploitation, address it through semi-supervised DRE-based optimization in sampling and fixed-pool scenarios, and demonstrate empirical effectiveness. The Protein results provide additional support without redefining these claims.

C2.justification: The exploration–exploitation interpretation, sampling and margin dependence, limitations of applying existing theory to sequential optimization, and pool-size computational limitations are retained. The impact statement moves from Appendix J to the main text without substantive revision.

D1.justification: v4 Section 5 explicitly specifies five initial points for every experiment; v3 specifies five points for its illustrative Figure 1 setup but lacks this general statement. v4 also removes the promise to release the implementation upon publication, without replacement code-access information. Other implementation details are retained.

R1.justification: v4 adds Jang et al. (2024), Model fusion through Bayesian optimization in language model fine-tuning, as an application example in the introduction and references. Positioning relative to BORE, LFBO, and semi-supervised learning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Baseline descriptions move from Appendix D.1 into Section 5, and the impact statement moves into the main text. Limited wording edits, expanded abbreviations, and revised equation introductions accompany these moves; the overall argument and section sequence remain stable.

P2.justification: The single-column preprint becomes a conference document with two-column main text and references, substantially changing typography, equation displays, and figure placement and sizing. Figure 5 gains a fourth panel; the MNIST examples become a separate appendix figure; and the runtime plots move to Appendix G.

improvement.justification: Adding Protein results resolves v3's mismatch between its four-dataset description and three listed and plotted Tabular datasets, modestly improving empirical completeness. Explicit initialization information and more accessible baseline descriptions improve clarity. Removing the code-release pledge weakens the reproducibility commitment, although neither PDF supplies implementation access. The net improvement is limited: the method, theoretical support, existing results, and limitations remain unchanged.
